content: Cytrel is a cellulose-based material that serves as a substitute for tobacco in certain low-tar cigarette brands. Notably, it constitutes 25% of the Silk Cut cigarette brand. The development of a tobacco replacement for cigarettes began in the 1950s, with the primary goal of reducing the presence of harmful components found in tobacco smoke. Cytrel was created by the Celanese Fiber Marketing Company. The development process for this fiber was challenging, as scientists faced significant difficulties in achieving acceptable properties for smoking, taste, and manufacturing. Despite these challenges, Cytrel's lower density compared to tobacco made it a useful bulking agent, which encouraged continued development efforts. After undergoing five revisions, the Celanese Fiber Marketing Company introduced Type 308 Cytrel to the market. This product became one of the New Smoking Materials (NSM) that gained popularity during the 1970s.
